item.title: Draft Cabinet Order and Ministerial Ordinance amendments to local government fee standards
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications proposed amendments to the Cabinet Order on Standards for Local Government Fees and its implementing Ministerial Ordinance, revising standard amounts to reflect prices, personnel costs and changes in administrative work. Examples include increasing childcare worker examination fees from JPY 12,700 to JPY 13,800, childcare worker registration application review fees from JPY 4,200 to JPY 6,100, and photograph replacement fees for hazardous materials handler and fire defense equipment officer licenses from JPY 1,600 to JPY 1,800. Other excerpted changes cover entertainment-business manager training, outdoor tank installation application reviews, fire equipment training, assistant nurse examinations, explosives safety examinations, administrative scrivener examinations, and reduced weapon-possession application review fees for foreign entrants participating in international competitions. The proposed Cabinet Order commencement is April 1, 2027, except for hazardous materials handler licenses, fire defense equipment officer licenses and examinations on May 1, 2027, and administrative scrivener examinations on April 1, 2028; the proposed Ministerial Ordinance commencement is May 1, 2027. A ministry announcement dated November 12, 2026 described the consultation scheduled from November 13, 2026 to December 14, 2026, with the listing specifying a deadline of 23:59 JST. item.title: Draft fisheries ordinances and new notice on foreign-operated recreational fishing vessels
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Ministerial Ordinance would amend implementing rules on foreign fishing and fishing in Japan's exclusive economic zone, clarifying the scope of minor harvesting using vessels of at least three gross tons, including recreational fishing vessels owned by foreign-managed Japanese corporations and foreign sole proprietors. It would also expressly allow qualifying permanent residents and other persons excluded from the statutory definition of foreigners to supervise such harvesting, reorganize gear categories, and include harvesting by bare hands. The excerpts state that the proposed vessel treatment would not change the definition of a Japanese vessel under the Ship Act. A proposed new Notice would designate vessels under Article 2(7) of the Act on Regulation of Fishing Operations by Foreign Nationals, but the supplied excerpts do not establish its precise designation criteria. The Fisheries Agency published the proposals for public comment on 2026-11-13; the stated deadline was 2026-12-12 23:59 JST. item.title: Draft Notice Amendment on Forest-Absorption J-Credits for Greenhouse Gas Reporting
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Notice amendment would add an entity's own efforts to preserve and enhance greenhouse gas absorption through forest management and conservation to the J-Credit scheme definition in item 4 of the domestic certified emission reductions notice. It would amend Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of the Environment Notice No. 3 of March 2010, supporting reporting by specified emitters under the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 117 of 1998). The explanatory document states that related instruments already provide for using forest-absorption credits from an entity's own efforts to adjust its own adjusted emissions; this draft would align the credit-definition notice with those provisions. The Ministry of the Environment and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry published the draft for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. Issuance of the Notice is planned for January 2027, with application planned from April 1, 2027; these are proposed dates, not confirmed implementation. item.title: Draft Ministerial Ordinance on Identity Checks for Voluntary My Number Account Management
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Ministerial Ordinance would amend the enforcement regulations for the Act on Management of Deposit and Savings Accounts Using Individual Numbers Based on Depositors' Wishes, revising identity checks by financial institutions and similar entities. For individuals attending in person, the draft would generally require chip-reading for chip-equipped identification and non-forwardable mailing for specified other documents; it would retain the existing photo-ID method for short-stay foreign nationals, diplomats and others for whom the revised methods are difficult. For remote checks, it would abolish specified methods using photographed ID images or mailed copies, retain a route using original anti-forgery documents, and preserve specified alternatives for nonresident foreign nationals and others; mailed corporate identification would generally require originals, with copies still permitted for foreign corporations. The Digital Agency's Digital Society Common Functions Group published the draft for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. The explanatory document states a proposed commencement date of April 1, 2027; this is a draft, not a confirmed enacted change. item.title: Draft Digital Agency Ordinance Revising Identity Checks for Public-Benefit Account Registration
item.description: AI summary: The Digital Agency published a draft amending ordinance for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST and proposed commencement on 2027-04-01. It would amend the implementing rules (Digital Agency Ordinance No. 10 of 2021) under Article 18 of the Act on Registration of Deposit and Savings Accounts for Prompt and Reliable Implementation of Public Benefit Payments (Act No. 38 of 2021). For financial institutions and similar entities verifying individual depositors in person, the proposal would require reading chip data when chip-equipped identification is presented; identification without a photograph would also require sending application-related documents by non-forwardable mail or equivalent, while non-chip identification would require such mailing and, if without a photograph, anti-forgery safeguards. For remote verification, it would abolish methods based on identification images photographed using institution-provided software or submitted identification copies, while retaining methods involving original anti-forgery-protected documents for depositors without chip-equipped identification and preserving specified alternatives for depositors who have moved overseas. The listed responsible office is the Digital Agency, Digital Society Common Functions Group.
